title: What I Got Wrong About Leadership
author: Jeff Matlow
source: The Best Leadership Newsletter Ever, January 5, 2026
summary: Jeff Matlow, who started three acquired companies, learned leadership through failure rather than natural talent, confessing critical mistakes including talking over listening, confusing being right with being smart, and avoiding hard conversations that create stronger teams. Wisdom came from repeatedly failing and noticing better doors existed. His transformation from lousy leader came through awareness of defensive moments, asking questions instead of pronouncing answers, and learning that discomfort creates culture. Leaders who hire for skillset while ignoring mindset and culture create technically competent but culturally broken teams incapable of motivation or lasting impact. Leadership breakthroughs come through noticing alarms earlier rather than sudden transformation.
points: Matlow started three companies that sold but confesses he was a lousy leader for most of his career, battling imposter syndrome without mentoring.
Talking more than listening, winning arguments while losing rooms, and avoiding accountability diffused the impact of his intelligence and effort.
Leaders who hire for skillset while ignoring mindset and culture create technically competent but culturally broken teams incapable of motivation.
Avoiding hard conversations to be nice actually shelters small problems until they swell into catastrophes that derail organizations and drain leaders.
Leadership breakthroughs come through noticing alarms earlier and becoming aware of moments where you feel defensive, rushed, or unsure rather than sudden transformation.
quotes: I didn't learn the leadership lessons I teach because I was always good at them. I learned them because I was a lousy leader for a long time.
I could win the argument and still lose the room. Being correct doesn't create a committed team. It just creates compliance. And compliance never turns into motivation.
I hired people who could do the work, but I ignored their ability to work well with others. I learned the hard way that culture is always more important than competence.
Leadership rarely breaks all at once. It erodes in small, subtle ways until you're left wondering what the hell went wrong.

Wisdom doesn't come from doing things right the first time. It comes from doing it wrong enough times to finally notice there is a different door with a different solution.” Archived from The Best Leadership Newsletter Ever on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
